Theorem
[Minimal positive heat kernel on complete manifolds] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0421, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0422, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0423, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0424, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0425 ↗ def:chow-ii-dirichlet-heat-kernel ↗ lem:chow-ii-duhamel-boundary ↗ thm:chow-ii-hopf-boundary-point 1. appe:1.14\group Heat Kernels

On every complete noncompact manifold, an exhaustion by compact regular domains and their Dirichlet kernels gives an increasing limit $h=\sup _i h_i$. This is a smooth, positive, symmetric, minimal positive fundamental solution. If $u$ solves the heat equation with uniformly bounded $L^1$ norm, then on every compact $K\times [t_0,T)$ all spatial derivatives of $u$ are uniformly bounded (the local estimate used to pass to the limit).
